prediction_check: §P7-14(c) named 3 entries in advance; the sweep caught 3 of them
corpse_note: mine.py's own docstring records an earlier build handing F10.7 (the 11 y solar cycle, 1.92 cycles in this window) a p at the resolution floor with z = 32. S-15(c) retroactively explains that corpse, which is the best evidence a new rule can have (§P7-14(c)).
orthogonality_note: S-15(c) is ORTHOGONAL to the S-15 power floor. A feature can pass a_min() and fail this, which is exactly what happened to the two Tranche A control rows. Amplitude floors are about N; this is about identifiability, and no N repairs it.

period_scan_grid.disposition: REPORTED, NOT CLAMPED. The period grid is a DECLARED config value; narrowing it is a new declaration and a new config hash (§P6-3 rule 5), not a build-time fix. Any peak the scan reports above 2572 d must carry the UNMEASURABLE-BY-WINDOW verdict.

what_this_does_not_do: an UNMEASURABLE-BY-WINDOW feature is scored NEITHER WAY. It is not a null, it may not be counted as one, and it may not be counted as a detection either. It is reported in the headline fraction and removed from both numerators.
